after: The cross arms always stay perpendicular to each other and to their own shaft, so the output must follow **tan θ₂ = cos β · tan θ₁**, which is exactly the relation the model computes. Differentiating gives **ω₂/ω₁ = cos β / (1 − sin²β · sin²θ₁)**: the gain is **cos β** at θ₁ = 0° (0.906 at β = 25°) and **1/cos β** at θ₁ = 90° (1.103). The speed ratio therefore swings twice per turn between these two limits, even though both shafts complete exactly one turn together. At β = 0° the motion is uniform. Real drivelines pair two joints in phase to cancel the fluctuation. Beyond 40° the yoke ears would hit each other, so the control rejects that angle.
title: Universal joint · transmission at an angle
before: A **Cardan (Hooke) joint** passes rotation between two shafts that meet at an angle β. Each shaft ends in a fork-shaped **yoke**; the yokes are linked by a **cross** whose two perpendicular arms pivot in bearings in the yoke ears. Drag **β**, then play the rotation and watch the output angle θ₂ lead and lag the input angle θ₁.
caption: A sectioned Cardan joint: an input yoke and an output yoke linked by an orange cross with four trunnions in needle cups, each shaft carried by a pillow block cut open to its axis. The output support swivels on a protractor arm to set the shaft angle β; playback reveals the non-uniform output speed.
